part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: PART II HOW JASON LOST HIS SANDAL IN ANAUROS

translation.en: Part 2: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
translation.kr: [제2부: 이아손이 아나우로스 강에서 샌들을 잃어버리다]

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And ten years came and went, and Jason was grown to be a mighty man. Some of his fellows were gone, and some were growing up by his side. Asclepius was gone into Peloponnese to work his wondrous cures on men; and some say he used to raise the dead to life.  And Heracles was gone to Thebes to fulfil those famous labours which have become a proverb among men.  And Peleus had married a sea-nymph, and his wedding is famous to this day.  And Æneas was gone home to Troy, and many a noble tale you will read of him, and of all the other gallant heroes, the scholars of Cheiron the just.  And it happened on a day that Jason stood on the mountain, and looked north and south and east and west; and Cheiron stood by him and watched him, for he knew that the time was come.

translation.en: Ten years passed, and Jason grew into a mighty man.
translation.kr: 십 년의 세월이 흘러 이아손은 건장한 청년으로 자라났습니다.

translation.en: Some of his friends had left, while others grew up alongside him.
translation.kr: 그의 친구들 중 일부는 떠났고, 일부는 그의 곁에서 함께 성장했습니다.

translation.en: Asclepius traveled to the Peloponnese to perform wondrous cures.
translation.kr: 아스클레피오스는 펠로폰네소스로 가서 놀라운 의술을 펼쳤습니다.

translation.en: Some say he even raised the dead back to life.
translation.kr: 어떤 이들은 그가 죽은 자를 되살리기도 했다고 말합니다.

translation.en: Heracles went to Thebes to complete his legendary labors.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스는 테베로 떠나 훗날 전설이 된 과업들을 수행했습니다.

translation.en: Peleus married a sea-nymph, and his wedding remains famous today.
translation.kr: 펠레우스는 바다의 요정과 결혼했고, 그 결혼식은 오늘날까지도 유명합니다.

translation.en: Aeneas returned home to Troy.
translation.kr: 아이네이아스는 고향인 트로이로 돌아갔습니다.

translation.en: You will read many noble tales of him and the other gallant heroes.
translation.kr: 여러분은 그를 비롯해 다른 훌륭한 영웅들의 이야기를 많이 읽게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: One day, Jason stood on the mountain, gazing in all directions.
translation.kr: 어느 날, 이아손은 산 위에 서서 사방을 둘러보았습니다.

translation.en: Chiron stood beside him and watched, knowing the time had come.
translation.kr: 케이론은 그의 곁에 서서 때가 왔음을 알고 그를 지켜보았습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And Jason looked and saw the plains of Thessaly, where the Lapithai breed their horses; and the lake of Boibé, and the stream which runs northward to Peneus and Tempe; and he looked north, and saw the mountain wall which guards the Magnesian shore; Olympus, the seat of the Immortals, and Ossa, and Pelion, where he stood. Then he looked east and saw the bright blue sea, which stretched away for ever toward the dawn.  Then he looked south, and saw a pleasant land, with white-walled towns and farms, nestling along the shore of a land-locked bay, while the smoke rose blue among the trees; and he knew it for the bay of Pagasai, and the rich lowlands of Hæmonia, and Iolcos by the sea.

translation.en: Jason looked and saw the plains of Thessaly.
translation.kr: 이아손은 라피타이족이 말을 기르는 테살리아 평원을 보았습니다.

translation.en: He saw the lake of Boibe and the stream running north to Peneus.
translation.kr: 보이베 호수와 페네이오스 강 쪽으로 북상하는 시냇물도 보였습니다.

translation.en: Looking north, he saw the mountain wall guarding the Magnesian shore.
translation.kr: 북쪽으로는 마그네시아 해안을 지키는 산맥이 보였습니다.

translation.en: He saw Olympus, the seat of the gods, along with Ossa and Pelion.
translation.kr: 신들의 거처인 올림포스와 오사 산, 그리고 자신이 서 있는 펠리온 산도 보았습니다.

translation.en: He looked east and saw the bright blue sea stretching toward the dawn.
translation.kr: 동쪽을 보자 새벽을 향해 끝없이 펼쳐진 밝고 푸른 바다가 있었습니다.

translation.en: To the south lay a pleasant land with white-walled towns and farms.
translation.kr: 남쪽으로는 하얀 성벽의 마을과 농장이 있는 아름다운 땅이 펼쳐졌습니다.

translation.en: They nestled along the shore of a land-locked bay.
translation.kr: 그곳은 육지로 둘러싸인 만의 해안을 따라 자리 잡고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Blue smoke rose among the trees.
translation.kr: 나무들 사이로는 푸른 연기가 피어올랐습니다.

translation.en: He recognized the bay of Pagasai and the rich lowlands of Haemonia.
translation.kr: 그는 그곳이 파가사이 만과 하이모니아의 비옥한 저지대임을 알았습니다.

translation.en: He also saw Iolcos by the sea.
translation.kr: 그리고 바닷가에 있는 이올코스도 보았습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then he sighed, and asked, ‘Is it true what the heroes tell me—that I am heir of that fair land?’

translation.en: Then he sighed and asked a question.
translation.kr: 그러자 그는 한숨을 쉬며 물었습니다.

translation.en: Is it true what the heroes tell me?
translation.kr: 영웅들이 제게 해준 말이 사실입니까?

translation.en: Am I the heir of that fair land?
translation.kr: 제가 저 아름다운 땅의 후계자라는 것 말입니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘And what good would it be to you, Jason, if you were heir of that fair land?’

translation.en: And what good would it be to you, Jason?
translation.kr: 네가 저 아름다운 땅의 후계자라면 네게 무슨 소용이 있겠느냐, 이아손?

translation.en: What if you were the heir of that fair land?
translation.kr: 네가 저 아름다운 땅의 후계자라고 해도 말이다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘I would take it and keep it.’

translation.en: I would take it and keep it.
translation.kr: 제가 그곳을 차지하고 지키겠습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘A strong man has taken it and kept it long.  Are you stronger than Pelias the terrible?’

translation.en: A strong man has taken it and kept it long.
translation.kr: 강한 자가 이미 그곳을 차지하고 오랫동안 지켜왔단다.

translation.en: Are you stronger than Pelias the terrible?
translation.kr: 네가 무시무시한 펠리아스보다 더 강하단 말이냐?

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘I can try my strength with his,’ said Jason; but Cheiron sighed, and said—

translation.en: I can try my strength with his, said Jason.
translation.kr: 그와 제 힘을 겨루어 볼 수 있습니다, 라고 이아손이 말했습니다.

translation.en: But Chiron sighed and replied.
translation.kr: 하지만 케이론은 한숨을 쉬며 대답했습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘You have many a danger to go through before you rule in Iolcos by the sea: many a danger and many a woe; and strange troubles in strange lands, such as man never saw before.’

translation.en: You have many a danger to face before you rule in Iolcos.
translation.kr: 네가 바닷가 이올코스를 다스리기 전까지 수많은 위험을 겪어야 할 것이다.

translation.en: You will face much woe and strange troubles in foreign lands.
translation.kr: 낯선 땅에서 지금껏 본 적 없는 시련과 슬픔을 마주하게 될 것이다.

translation.en: No man has ever seen such trials before.
translation.kr: 인간이 한 번도 겪어보지 못한 고난들이지.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘The happier I,’ said Jason, ‘to see what man never saw before.’

translation.en: Then I am the happier, said Jason.
translation.kr: 그러면 제가 더 행복한 사람이겠네요, 라고 이아손이 말했습니다.

translation.en: I will see what no man has ever seen before.
translation.kr: 아무도 본 적 없는 것을 보게 될 테니까요.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And Cheiron sighed again, and said, ‘The eaglet must leave the nest when it is fledged.  Will you go to Iolcos by the sea?  Then promise me two things before you go.’

translation.en: Chiron sighed again and spoke.
translation.kr: 케이론은 다시 한숨을 내쉬며 말했습니다.

translation.en: The eaglet must leave the nest when its feathers grow.
translation.kr: 새끼 독수리는 깃털이 자라면 둥지를 떠나야 하는 법이지.

translation.en: Will you go to Iolcos by the sea?
translation.kr: 바닷가 이올코스로 가려느냐?

translation.en: Then promise me two things before you go.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 떠나기 전에 내게 두 가지를 약속해 다오.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Jason promised, and Cheiron answered, ‘Speak harshly to no soul whom you may meet, and stand by the word which you shall speak.’

translation.en: Jason promised, and Chiron answered.
translation.kr: 이아손이 약속하자 케이론이 대답했습니다.

translation.en: Speak harshly to no soul whom you may meet.
translation.kr: 네가 만나는 그 누구에게도 거칠게 말하지 마라.

translation.en: And stand by the word which you shall speak.
translation.kr: 그리고 네가 한 말은 반드시 지켜야 한다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Jason wondered why Cheiron asked this of him; but he knew that the Centaur was a prophet, and saw things long before they came.  So he promised, and leapt down the mountain, to take his fortune like a man.

translation.en: Jason wondered why Chiron asked this of him.
translation.kr: 이아손은 케이론이 왜 이런 부탁을 하는지 궁금했습니다.

translation.en: But he knew the Centaur was a prophet who saw the future.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 이 켄타우로스가 먼 미래를 보는 예언자라는 것을 알고 있었습니다.

translation.en: So he promised and leapt down the mountain.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 약속을 하고 산을 뛰어 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: He went to seek his fortune like a man.
translation.kr: 그는 사내답게 자신의 운명을 찾아 나섰습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: He went down through the arbutus thickets, and across the downs of thyme, till he came to the vineyard walls, and the pomegranates and the olives in the glen; and among the olives roared Anauros, all foaming with a summer flood.

translation.en: He went down through the arbutus thickets.
translation.kr: 그는 산딸기나무 숲을 지나 아래로 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: He crossed the hills of thyme to the vineyard walls.
translation.kr: 백리향이 피어 있는 언덕을 건너 포도밭 담장에 이르렀습니다.

translation.en: He passed the pomegranates and olives in the glen.
translation.kr: 그는 계곡의 석류나무와 올리브나무 사이를 지났습니다.

translation.en: Among the olives roared the Anauros river, foaming with a summer flood.
translation.kr: 올리브나무 사이로 아나우로스 강이 여름 홍수로 거품을 일으키며 으르렁거리고 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And on the bank of Anauros sat a woman, all wrinkled, gray, and old; her head shook palsied on her breast, and her hands shook palsied on her knees; and when she saw Jason, she spoke whining, ‘Who will carry me across the flood?’

translation.en: On the bank of Anauros sat a woman.
translation.kr: 아나우로스 강변에는 한 여인이 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: She was wrinkled, gray, and old.
translation.kr: 그녀는 주름지고 머리가 희끗희끗한 노파였습니다.

translation.en: Her head shook palsied on her breast.
translation.kr: 그녀의 머리는 마비된 듯 가슴 위에서 떨렸습니다.

translation.en: Her hands shook palsied on her knees.
translation.kr: 그녀의 두 손도 무릎 위에서 심하게 떨렸습니다.

translation.en: When she saw Jason, she spoke whining.
translation.kr: 그녀는 이아손을 보자 징징거리며 말했습니다.

translation.en: Who will carry me across the flood?
translation.kr: 누가 이 홍수를 건너게 날 좀 업어다 줄꼬?

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Jason was bold and hasty, and was just going to leap into the flood: and yet he thought twice before he leapt, so loud roared the torrent down, all brown from the mountain rains, and silver-veined with melting snow; while underneath he could hear the boulders rumbling like the tramp of horsemen or the roll of wheels, as they ground along the narrow channel, and shook the rocks on which he stood.

translation.en: Jason was bold and hasty.
translation.kr: 이아손은 용감하고 성급했습니다.

translation.en: He was just going to leap into the flood.
translation.kr: 그는 막 급류 속으로 뛰어들려던 참이었습니다.

translation.en: But he thought twice before he leapt.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 뛰어들기 전에 다시 한번 생각했습니다.

translation.en: The torrent roared loudly down the mountain.
translation.kr: 급류가 산 아래로 큰 소리를 내며 쏟아져 내렸기 때문입니다.

translation.en: It was brown from the rains and silver-veined with melting snow.
translation.kr: 비 때문에 물빛은 갈색이었고, 녹은 눈이 섞여 은빛 줄기를 이루고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Underneath, he could hear the boulders rumbling.
translation.kr: 물속에서는 커다란 바위들이 굴러가는 소리가 들렸습니다.

translation.en: It sounded like the tramp of horsemen or the roll of wheels.
translation.kr: 마치 기병대의 발소리나 마차가 굴러가는 소리 같았습니다.

translation.en: They ground along the narrow channel and shook the rocks beneath his feet.
translation.kr: 바위들은 좁은 수로를 따라 부딪히며 그가 서 있는 바위마저 흔들었습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: But the old woman whined all the more, ‘I am weak and old, fair youth. For Hera’s sake, carry me over the torrent.’

translation.en: But the old woman whined all the more.
translation.kr: 하지만 노파는 더욱더 징징거리며 말했습니다.

translation.en: I am weak and old, fair youth.
translation.kr: 잘생긴 젊은이, 나는 늙고 힘이 없다네.

translation.en: For Hera’s sake, carry me over the torrent.
translation.kr: 헤라 여신을 보아서라도 나를 업고 이 급류를 건너주게.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And Jason was going to answer her scornfully, when Cheiron’s words came to his mind.

translation.en: Jason was going to answer her scornfully.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그녀에게 차갑게 대답하려 했습니다.

translation.en: But Chiron’s words came to his mind.
translation.kr: 그때 케이론이 해준 말이 떠올랐습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: So he said, ‘For Hera’s sake, the Queen of the Immortals on Olympus, I will carry you over the torrent, unless we both are drowned midway.’

translation.en: So he said, For Hera’s sake, the Queen of Olympus, I will carry you.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 말했습니다. 올림포스의 여왕이신 헤라 여신을 위해 제가 업어드리겠습니다.

translation.en: I will carry you over the torrent, unless we both drown midway.
translation.kr: 우리 둘 다 중간에 물에 빠져 죽지 않는다면 이 급류를 건너게 해드리죠.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then the old dame leapt upon his back, as nimbly as a goat; and Jason staggered in, wondering; and the first step was up to his knees.

translation.en: Then the old dame leapt upon his back as nimbly as a goat.
translation.kr: 그러자 노파는 염소처럼 날렵하게 그의 등 위로 뛰어올랐습니다.

translation.en: Jason staggered in, wondering at her speed.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그녀의 민첩함에 놀라며 비틀거렸습니다.

translation.en: The first step was up to his knees.
translation.kr: 첫걸음을 내딛자 물이 무릎까지 차올랐습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: The first step was up to his knees, and the second step was up to his waist; and the stones rolled about his feet, and his feet slipped about the stones; so he went on staggering, and panting, while the old woman cried from off his back—

translation.en: The first step was up to his knees.
translation.kr: 첫걸음에는 물이 무릎까지 왔습니다.

translation.en: The second step was up to his waist.
translation.kr: 두 번째 걸음에는 허리까지 차올랐습니다.

translation.en: Stones rolled about his feet, and he slipped often.
translation.kr: 발밑으로 돌들이 굴러다녔고, 그는 자주 미끄러졌습니다.

translation.en: He went on staggering and panting.
translation.kr: 그는 비틀거리고 숨을 헐떡이며 앞으로 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, the old woman cried from his back.
translation.kr: 그러는 동안 노파는 그의 등에 업혀 소리쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘Fool, you have wet my mantle!  Do you make game of poor old souls like me?’

translation.en: Fool, you have wet my mantle!
translation.kr: 이 바보야, 내 망토가 다 젖었잖느냐!

translation.en: Do you make game of poor old souls like me?
translation.kr: 나 같은 불쌍한 늙은이를 놀리는 게냐?

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Jason had half a mind to drop her, and let her get through the torrent by herself; but Cheiron’s words were in his mind, and he said only, ‘Patience, mother; the best horse may stumble some day.’

translation.en: Jason had half a mind to drop her.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그녀를 물속에 떨어뜨려 버릴까 생각했습니다.

translation.en: He wanted to let her cross the torrent alone.
translation.kr: 그녀 혼자 급류를 건너게 내버려두고 싶었습니다.

translation.en: But Chiron’s words were in his mind.
translation.kr: 하지만 케이론의 말이 마음속에 맴돌았습니다.

translation.en: He only said, Patience, mother.
translation.kr: 그는 그저 이렇게 말했습니다. 참으십시오, 할머니.

translation.en: Even the best horse may stumble some day.
translation.kr: 가장 좋은 말도 가끔은 비틀거리는 법이니까요.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: At last he staggered to the shore, and set her down upon the bank; and a strong man he needed to have been, or that wild water he never would have crossed.

translation.en: At last he staggered to the shore.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 비틀거리며 반대편 기슭에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: He set her down upon the bank.
translation.kr: 그는 강둑에 그녀를 내려놓았습니다.

translation.en: He needed to be a very strong man to cross that wild water.
translation.kr: 그가 엄청나게 힘이 센 사내가 아니었다면, 그 거친 물살을 결코 건너지 못했을 것입니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: He lay panting awhile upon the bank, and then leapt up to go upon his journey; but he cast one look at the old woman, for he thought, ‘She should thank me once at least.’

translation.en: He lay panting awhile upon the bank.
translation.kr: 그는 한동안 강둑에 누워 숨을 헐떡였습니다.

translation.en: Then he leapt up to go on his journey.
translation.kr: 그러고는 길을 떠나기 위해 벌떡 일어났습니다.

translation.en: But he cast one look at the old woman.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 노파를 한번 돌아보았습니다.

translation.en: He thought she should thank him at least once.
translation.kr: 적어도 한 번은 고맙다는 말을 해야 한다고 생각했기 때문입니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And as he looked, she grew fairer than all women, and taller than all men on earth; and her garments shone like the summer sea, and her jewels like the stars of heaven; and over her forehead was a veil woven of the golden clouds of sunset; and through the veil she looked down on him, with great soft heifer’s eyes; with great eyes, mild and awful, which filled all the glen with light.

translation.en: As he looked, she grew fairer than all women.
translation.kr: 그가 바라보자, 그녀는 세상의 어떤 여인보다 아름답게 변했습니다.

translation.en: She stood taller than all men on earth.
translation.kr: 그녀는 지상의 어떤 남자보다도 키가 컸습니다.

translation.en: Her garments shone like the summer sea.
translation.kr: 그녀의 옷은 여름 바다처럼 빛났습니다.

translation.en: Her jewels sparkled like the stars of heaven.
translation.kr: 그녀의 보석은 하늘의 별처럼 반짝였습니다.

translation.en: A veil woven of golden sunset clouds covered her forehead.
translation.kr: 해 질 녘의 황금빛 구름으로 짠 베일이 그녀의 이마를 덮고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Through the veil, she looked down on him.
translation.kr: 그 베일 너머로 그녀가 그를 내려다보았습니다.

translation.en: She had great, soft eyes like a heifer.
translation.kr: 그녀는 암소처럼 크고 부드러운 눈망울을 가졌습니다.

translation.en: Her great eyes were mild yet awful, filling the glen with light.
translation.kr: 온화하면서도 두려움을 자아내는 그녀의 커다란 눈은 온 계곡을 빛으로 채웠습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And Jason fell upon his knees, and hid his face between his hands.

translation.en: Jason fell upon his knees and hid his face between his hands.
translation.kr: 이아손은 무릎을 꿇고 두 손으로 얼굴을 가렸습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And she spoke, ‘I am the Queen of Olympus, Hera the wife of Zeus.  As thou hast done to me, so will I do to thee.  Call on me in the hour of need, and try if the Immortals can forget.’

translation.en: And she spoke to him.
translation.kr: 그리고 그녀가 그에게 말했습니다.

translation.en: I am the Queen of Olympus, Hera the wife of Zeus.
translation.kr: 나는 올림포스의 여왕이자 제우스의 아내인 헤라이다.

translation.en: As you have done to me, so will I do to you.
translation.kr: 네가 내게 한 대로 나도 너에게 갚아주겠다.

translation.en: Call on me in the hour of need.
translation.kr: 어려운 일이 생기면 나를 부르거라.

translation.en: You will see if the gods ever forget.
translation.kr: 신들이 은혜를 잊는지 아닌지 알게 될 것이다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: [Picture: Jason and Hera]

translation.en: [Picture: Jason and Hera]
translation.kr: [그림: 이아손과 헤라]

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And when Jason looked up, she rose from off the earth, like a pillar of tall white cloud, and floated away across the mountain peaks, toward Olympus the holy hill.

translation.en: When Jason looked up, she rose from the earth.
translation.kr: 이아손이 고개를 들었을 때, 그녀는 땅에서 떠올랐습니다.

translation.en: She looked like a pillar of tall white cloud.
translation.kr: 마치 길게 뻗은 하얀 구름 기둥 같았습니다.

translation.en: She floated away across the mountain peaks toward holy Olympus.
translation.kr: 그녀는 산봉우리들을 지나 신성한 언덕 올림포스를 향해 날아갔습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then a great fear fell on Jason: but after a while he grew light of heart; and he blessed old Cheiron, and said, ‘Surely the Centaur is a prophet, and guessed what would come to pass, when he bade me speak harshly to no soul whom I might meet.’

translation.en: A great fear fell on Jason, but soon his heart grew light.
translation.kr: 이아손은 큰 두려움에 사로잡혔지만, 이내 마음이 가벼워졌습니다.

translation.en: He blessed old Chiron for his wise advice.
translation.kr: 그는 현명한 조언을 해준 늙은 케이론에게 감사했습니다.

translation.en: He knew the Centaur was a true prophet.
translation.kr: 그는 그 켄타우로스가 진정한 예언자라는 것을 알았습니다.

translation.en: Chiron had guessed what would happen when he gave his warning.
translation.kr: 케이론은 거칠게 말하지 말라고 경고했을 때 이미 이 일이 일어날 것을 짐작했던 것입니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then he went down toward Iolcos; and as he walked he found that he had lost one of his sandals in the flood.

translation.en: Then he went down toward Iolcos.
translation.kr: 그리고 그는 이올코스를 향해 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: As he walked, he realized he had lost a sandal in the flood.
translation.kr: 걷다가 그는 홍수 속에서 샌들 한 짝을 잃어버렸다는 것을 알게 되었습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And as he went through the streets, the people came out to look at him, so tall and fair was he; but some of the elders whispered together; and at last one of them stopped Jason, and called to him, ‘Fair lad, who are you, and whence come you; and what is your errand in the town?’

translation.en: He went through the streets, and the people came out to look.
translation.kr: 그가 거리를 지날 때, 사람들이 나와 그를 구경했습니다.

translation.en: He was so tall and fair that they stared at him.
translation.kr: 그가 너무나 훤칠하고 잘생겼기 때문에 모두가 그를 빤히 쳐다보았습니다.

translation.en: Some of the elders whispered together.
translation.kr: 어르신들 몇몇이 모여 수군거렸습니다.

translation.en: At last, one of them stopped Jason and called to him.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들 중 한 명이 이아손을 멈춰 세우고 물었습니다.

translation.en: Fair lad, who are you, and where do you come from?
translation.kr: 잘생긴 젊은이, 자네는 누구고 어디서 왔는가?

translation.en: What is your errand in the town?
translation.kr: 이 마을에는 무슨 일로 온 겐가?

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘My name, good father, is Jason, and I come from Pelion up above; and my errand is to Pelias your king; tell me then where his palace is.’

translation.en: My name, good father, is Jason.
translation.kr: 어르신, 제 이름은 이아손입니다.

translation.en: I come from Mount Pelion up above.
translation.kr: 저는 저 위 펠리온 산에서 왔습니다.

translation.en: My errand is to see Pelias, your king.
translation.kr: 이곳의 왕이신 펠리아스를 뵈러 왔지요.

translation.en: Tell me where his palace is.
translation.kr: 왕궁이 어디 있는지 알려주시겠습니까?

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: But the old man started, and grew pale, and said, ‘Do you not know the oracle, my son, that you go so boldly through the town with but one sandal on?’

translation.en: The old man started and grew pale.
translation.kr: 노인은 깜짝 놀라며 얼굴이 창백해졌습니다.

translation.en: Do you not know the oracle, my son?
translation.kr: 젊은이, 신탁에 대해 알지 못하는가?

translation.en: You walk so boldly through the town with only one sandal.
translation.kr: 샌들을 한 짝만 신은 채 이렇게 당당하게 마을을 활보하다니.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘I am a stranger here, and know of no oracle; but what of my one sandal? I lost the other in Anauros, while I was struggling with the flood.’

translation.en: I am a stranger here and know of no oracle.
translation.kr: 저는 이곳에 처음 와서 신탁에 대해서는 모릅니다.

translation.en: But what does my one sandal have to do with it?
translation.kr: 하지만 제 샌들 한 짝이 무슨 상관입니까?

translation.en: I lost the other in the Anauros flood.
translation.kr: 나머지 한 짝은 아나우로스의 급류와 싸우다 잃어버렸습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then the old man looked back to his companions; and one sighed, and another smiled; at last he said, ‘I will tell you, lest you rush upon your ruin unawares.  The oracle in Delphi has said that a man wearing one sandal should take the kingdom from Pelias, and keep it for himself. Therefore beware how you go up to his palace, for he is the fiercest and most cunning of all kings.’

translation.en: The old man looked back at his companions.
translation.kr: 노인은 뒤돌아 자신의 동료들을 보았습니다.

translation.en: One sighed, and another smiled.
translation.kr: 한 명은 한숨을 쉬었고, 다른 한 명은 미소를 지었습니다.

translation.en: At last he warned the young man.
translation.kr: 마침내 그가 젊은이에게 경고했습니다.

translation.en: I will tell you, so you do not rush to your ruin unawares.
translation.kr: 자네가 모르고 죽음의 길로 뛰어들지 않도록 말해주겠네.

translation.en: The oracle in Delphi made a prophecy.
translation.kr: 델포이의 신탁에서 예언을 내렸지.

translation.en: A man wearing one sandal would take the kingdom from Pelias.
translation.kr: 샌들을 한 짝만 신은 사내가 펠리아스에게서 왕국을 빼앗아 차지할 것이라고 말이네.

translation.en: So beware how you go up to his palace.
translation.kr: 그러니 왕궁으로 갈 때 조심하게.

translation.en: He is the fiercest and most cunning of all kings.
translation.kr: 그는 모든 왕 중에서 가장 잔인하고 교활한 자라네.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then Jason laughed a great laugh, like a war-horse in his pride.  ‘Good news, good father, both for you and me.  For that very end I came into the town.’

translation.en: Then Jason laughed a great laugh, like a proud war-horse.
translation.kr: 그러자 이아손은 기세등등한 군마처럼 크게 웃었습니다.

translation.en: Good news, good father, for both you and me.
translation.kr: 어르신과 저 모두에게 기쁜 소식이군요.

translation.en: For that is exactly why I came into the town.
translation.kr: 제가 이 마을에 온 목적이 바로 그것이니까요.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then he strode on toward the palace of Pelias, while all the people wondered at his bearing.

translation.en: Then he strode toward the palace of Pelias.
translation.kr: 그리고 그는 펠리아스의 왕궁을 향해 성큼성큼 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: All the people wondered at his bold bearing.
translation.kr: 모든 사람들이 그의 당당한 태도에 놀랐습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And he stood in the doorway and cried, ‘Come out, come out, Pelias the valiant, and fight for your kingdom like a man.’

translation.en: He stood in the doorway and shouted loud.
translation.kr: 그는 문간에 서서 큰 소리로 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Come out, Pelias the valiant!
translation.kr: 나와라, 용맹한 펠리아스여!

translation.en: Fight for your kingdom like a man.
translation.kr: 사내답게 당신의 왕국을 걸고 싸우자.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Pelias came out wondering, and ‘Who are you, bold youth?’ he cried.

translation.en: Pelias came out wondering and cried out.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 의아해하며 나와서 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Who are you, bold youth?
translation.kr: 너는 누구냐, 건방진 젊은이여?

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘I am Jason, the son of Æson, the heir of all this land.’

translation.en: I am Jason, the son of Aeson.
translation.kr: 나는 아이손의 아들 이아손이다.

translation.en: I am the true heir of all this land.
translation.kr: 이 모든 땅의 진정한 후계자다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then Pelias lifted up his hands and eyes, and wept, or seemed to weep; and blessed the heavens which had brought his nephew to him, never to leave him more.  ‘For,’ said he, ‘I have but three daughters, and no son to be my heir.  You shall be my heir then, and rule the kingdom after me, and marry whichsoever of my daughters you shall choose; though a sad kingdom you will find it, and whosoever rules it a miserable man.  But come in, come in, and feast.’

translation.en: Pelias lifted his hands and eyes and wept, or seemed to weep.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 두 손을 들고 눈을 치켜뜨며 울거나, 우는 척했습니다.

translation.en: He blessed the heavens for bringing his nephew to him.
translation.kr: 그는 조카를 자신에게 데려와 영원히 함께하게 해준 하늘을 축복했습니다.

translation.en: I have but three daughters and no son to be my heir, he said.
translation.kr: 내게는 딸만 셋뿐이고 후계자가 될 아들이 없단다, 라고 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: You shall be my heir and rule after me.
translation.kr: 네가 내 후계자가 되어 내 뒤를 이어 왕국을 다스려라.

translation.en: You may marry whichever of my daughters you choose.
translation.kr: 내 딸들 중 네가 원하는 아이와 결혼해도 좋다.

translation.en: Though you will find it a sad kingdom to rule.
translation.kr: 다스리기에 슬픈 왕국이라는 걸 알게 되겠지만 말이다.

translation.en: Whoever rules it will be a miserable man.
translation.kr: 누구든 이 왕국을 다스리는 자는 비참한 사람이 될 것이다.

translation.en: But come in, come in, and let us feast.
translation.kr: 하지만 들어오너라, 들어와서 연회를 즐기자.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: So he drew Jason in, whether he would or not, and spoke to him so lovingly and feasted him so well, that Jason’s anger passed; and after supper his three cousins came into the hall, and Jason thought that he should like well enough to have one of them for his wife.

translation.en: He drew Jason in, whether he wanted to or not.
translation.kr: 그는 이아손이 원하든 원하지 않든 그를 안으로 끌어들였습니다.

translation.en: He spoke lovingly and feasted him so well that Jason’s anger passed.
translation.kr: 그가 너무나 다정하게 말하며 성대하게 대접하자 이아손의 분노도 사그라들었습니다.

translation.en: After supper, his three cousins came into the hall.
translation.kr: 저녁 식사 후, 그의 세 사촌이 홀로 들어왔습니다.

translation.en: Jason thought he would gladly take one of them for his wife.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그들 중 한 명을 아내로 맞이하는 것도 괜찮겠다고 생각했습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: But at last he said to Pelias, ‘Why do you look so sad, my uncle?  And what did you mean just now when you said that this was a doleful kingdom, and its ruler a miserable man?’

translation.en: But at last he asked Pelias a question.
translation.kr: 하지만 마침내 그는 펠리아스에게 질문했습니다.

translation.en: Why do you look so sad, my uncle?
translation.kr: 숙부님, 왜 그렇게 슬퍼 보이십니까?

translation.en: What did you mean when you called this a doleful kingdom?
translation.kr: 아까 이 왕국을 슬픈 왕국이라 하신 건 무슨 뜻입니까?

translation.en: Why would its ruler be a miserable man?
translation.kr: 왜 이 왕국의 통치자가 비참한 사람이 된다는 것입니까?

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then Pelias sighed heavily again and again and again, like a man who had to tell some dreadful story, and was afraid to begin; but at last—

translation.en: Pelias sighed heavily, again and again.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 계속해서 깊은 한숨을 내쉬었습니다.

translation.en: He acted like a man afraid to tell a dreadful story.
translation.kr: 그는 끔찍한 이야기를 꺼내기 두려워하는 사람처럼 행동했습니다.

translation.en: But at last he spoke.
translation.kr: 그러다 마침내 입을 열었습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘For seven long years and more have I never known a quiet night; and no more will he who comes after me, till the golden fleece be brought home.’

translation.en: For seven long years, I have never known a quiet night.
translation.kr: 무려 7년이 넘도록 나는 단 하루도 편안한 밤을 보낸 적이 없다.

translation.en: Nor will the one who rules after me.
translation.kr: 내 뒤를 이을 통치자 역시 마찬가지일 것이다.

translation.en: We will not rest until the golden fleece is brought home.
translation.kr: 황금 양털을 고향으로 가져오기 전까지는 말이다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then he told Jason the story of Phrixus, and of the golden fleece; and told him, too, which was a lie, that Phrixus’ spirit tormented him, calling to him day and night.  And his daughters came, and told the same tale (for their father had taught them their parts), and wept, and said, ‘Oh who will bring home the golden fleece, that our uncle’s spirit may rest; and that we may have rest also, whom he never lets sleep in peace?’

translation.en: Then he told Jason the story of Phrixus and the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 그리고 그는 이아손에게 프릭소스와 황금 양털 이야기를 들려주었습니다.

translation.en: He lied that Phrixus’ spirit tormented him day and night.
translation.kr: 그는 프릭소스의 영혼이 밤낮으로 자신을 부르며 괴롭힌다고 거짓말을 했습니다.

translation.en: His daughters came and told the same tale.
translation.kr: 그의 딸들도 와서 같은 이야기를 했습니다.

translation.en: Their father had taught them their parts well.
translation.kr: 그들의 아버지가 미리 역할을 잘 가르쳐 두었기 때문입니다.

translation.en: They wept and asked who would bring home the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 그들은 울면서 누가 황금 양털을 고향으로 가져오겠냐며 물었습니다.

translation.en: They said it would let their uncle’s spirit rest.
translation.kr: 그렇게 해야만 삼촌의 영혼이 안식을 찾을 수 있다고 말했습니다.

translation.en: And then they, too, could finally sleep in peace.
translation.kr: 그래야 자신들도 마침내 편안하게 잠들 수 있다고 했습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Jason sat awhile, sad and silent; for he had often heard of that golden fleece; but he looked on it as a thing hopeless and impossible for any mortal man to win it.

translation.en: Jason sat awhile, sad and silent.
translation.kr: 이아손은 슬픔에 잠겨 한동안 말없이 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: He had often heard of that golden fleece.
translation.kr: 그도 황금 양털에 대해 종종 들은 적이 있었습니다.

translation.en: But he believed it impossible for any mortal man to win it.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 인간이 그것을 얻는 것은 불가능하다고 생각했습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: But when Pelias saw him silent, he began to talk of other things, and courted Jason more and more, speaking to him as if he was certain to be his heir, and asking his advice about the kingdom; till Jason, who was young and simple, could not help saying to himself, ‘Surely he is not the dark man whom people call him.  Yet why did he drive my father out?’  And he asked Pelias boldly, ‘Men say that you are terrible, and a man of blood; but I find you a kind and hospitable man; and as you are to me, so will I be to you.  Yet why did you drive my father out?’

translation.en: When Pelias saw him silent, he began to talk of other things.
translation.kr: 이아손이 아무 말도 하지 않자, 펠리아스는 다른 이야기를 꺼냈습니다.

translation.en: He courted Jason more and more.
translation.kr: 그는 더욱 이아손의 환심을 사려 했습니다.

translation.en: He spoke as if Jason were certain to be his heir.
translation.kr: 그는 이아손이 확실한 후계자인 것처럼 말했습니다.

translation.en: He even asked Jason’s advice about the kingdom.
translation.kr: 심지어 왕국의 일에 대해 이아손에게 조언을 구하기도 했습니다.

translation.en: Jason was young and simple, and he thought to himself.
translation.kr: 젊고 순진했던 이아손은 속으로 생각했습니다.

translation.en: Surely he is not the dark man people call him.
translation.kr: 사람들이 말하는 것처럼 사악한 분은 아니구나.

translation.en: Yet why did he drive my father out?
translation.kr: 그런데 왜 아버지를 쫓아내셨을까?

translation.en: So he boldly asked Pelias a direct question.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 펠리아스에게 대담하게 직설적인 질문을 던졌습니다.

translation.en: Men say you are terrible and a man of blood.
translation.kr: 사람들은 숙부님이 무시무시하고 잔인한 분이라고 말합니다.

translation.en: But I find you a kind and hospitable man.
translation.kr: 하지만 제가 보기엔 친절하고 환대해 주시는 분입니다.

translation.en: As you are to me, so will I be to you.
translation.kr: 숙부님이 제게 하신 만큼 저도 숙부님께 할 것입니다.

translation.en: Yet why did you drive my father out?
translation.kr: 하지만 왜 제 아버지를 쫓아내셨습니까?

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Pelias smiled, and sighed.  ‘Men have slandered me in that, as in all things.  Your father was growing old and weary, and he gave the kingdom up to me of his own will.  You shall see him to-morrow, and ask him; and he will tell you the same.’

translation.en: Pelias smiled and sighed.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 미소를 지으며 한숨을 쉬었습니다.

translation.en: Men have slandered me in that, as in all things.
translation.kr: 다른 모든 일과 마찬가지로 사람들이 나를 모함한 것이란다.

translation.en: Your father was growing old and weary.
translation.kr: 네 아버지는 늙고 지쳐가고 있었지.

translation.en: He gave the kingdom up to me of his own will.
translation.kr: 그래서 자신의 뜻으로 왕국을 내게 물려준 것이다.

translation.en: You shall see him tomorrow and ask him.
translation.kr: 내일 네 아버지를 만나 직접 물어보아라.

translation.en: He will tell you the exact same thing.
translation.kr: 그도 너에게 똑같이 말할 것이다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Jason’s heart leapt in him when he heard that he was to see his father; and he believed all that Pelias said, forgetting that his father might not dare to tell the truth.

translation.en: Jason’s heart leapt to hear he would see his father.
translation.kr: 아버지를 만나게 될 거라는 말에 이아손의 가슴이 뛰었습니다.

translation.en: He believed all that Pelias said.
translation.kr: 그는 펠리아스의 말을 모두 믿었습니다.

translation.en: He forgot his father might not dare tell the truth.
translation.kr: 아버지가 감히 진실을 말하지 못할 수도 있다는 사실은 잊어버렸습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘One thing more there is,’ said Pelias, ‘on which I need your advice; for, though you are young, I see in you a wisdom beyond your years. There is one neighbour of mine, whom I dread more than all men on earth. I am stronger than he now, and can command him; but I know that if he stay among us, he will work my ruin in the end.  Can you give me a plan, Jason, by which I can rid myself of that man?’

translation.en: There is one more thing, said Pelias.
translation.kr: 한 가지 더 물어볼 게 있단다, 라고 펠리아스가 말했습니다.

translation.en: I need your advice on this matter.
translation.kr: 이 문제에 대해 네 조언이 필요하구나.

translation.en: Though young, you show wisdom beyond your years.
translation.kr: 너는 비록 어리지만 나이에 비해 뛰어난 지혜를 가졌으니까.

translation.en: I have a neighbor whom I dread more than anyone else.
translation.kr: 내 이웃 중에 내가 세상 누구보다 두려워하는 자가 있단다.

translation.en: I am stronger than him now and can command him.
translation.kr: 지금은 내가 그보다 강해서 그에게 명령을 내릴 수 있지.

translation.en: But if he stays, he will ruin me in the end.
translation.kr: 하지만 그가 계속 여기 머문다면 결국 나를 파멸시킬 것이다.

translation.en: Can you give me a plan to rid myself of this man?
translation.kr: 이아손, 그 자를 쫓아낼 묘안이 없겠느냐?

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: After awhile Jason answered, half laughing, ‘Were I you, I would send him to fetch that same golden fleece; for if he once set forth after it you would never be troubled with him more.’

translation.en: After a while, Jason answered half-laughing.
translation.kr: 잠시 후 이아손은 반쯤 웃으며 대답했습니다.

translation.en: If I were you, I would send him to fetch the golden fleece.
translation.kr: 제가 숙부님이라면 그에게 황금 양털을 가져오라고 보내겠습니다.

translation.en: If he sets forth after it, he will never trouble you again.
translation.kr: 그가 그것을 찾으러 떠난다면 다시는 숙부님을 괴롭히지 못할 테니까요.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And at that a bitter smile came across Pelias’ lips, and a flash of wicked joy into his eyes; and Jason saw it, and started; and over his mind came the warning of the old man, and his own one sandal, and the oracle, and he saw that he was taken in a trap.

translation.en: A bitter smile crossed Pelias’ lips.
translation.kr: 펠리아스의 입가에 씁쓸한 미소가 번졌습니다.

translation.en: A flash of wicked joy appeared in his eyes.
translation.kr: 그의 눈에는 사악한 기쁨이 번뜩였습니다.

translation.en: Jason saw it and started in surprise.
translation.kr: 이아손은 그것을 보고 깜짝 놀랐습니다.

translation.en: He remembered the old man’s warning and his single sandal.
translation.kr: 그는 노인의 경고와 자신의 샌들 한 짝을 떠올렸습니다.

translation.en: He remembered the oracle and realized he was trapped.
translation.kr: 신탁을 기억해 낸 그는 자신이 덫에 빠졌음을 깨달았습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: But Pelias only answered gently, ‘My son, he shall be sent forthwith.’

translation.en: But Pelias only answered gently.
translation.kr: 하지만 펠리아스는 그저 부드럽게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: My son, he shall be sent immediately.
translation.kr: 내 아들아, 당장 그를 보내야겠구나.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘You mean me?’ cried Jason, starting up, ‘because I came here with one sandal?’  And he lifted his fist angrily, while Pelias stood up to him like a wolf at bay; and whether of the two was the stronger and the fiercer it would be hard to tell.

translation.en: You mean me? cried Jason, starting up.
translation.kr: 저를 말씀하시는 겁니까? 이아손이 벌떡 일어나며 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Is it because I came here with one sandal?
translation.kr: 제가 샌들을 한 짝만 신고 왔기 때문입니까?

translation.en: He lifted his fist angrily.
translation.kr: 그는 분노하며 주먹을 치켜들었습니다.

translation.en: Pelias stood up to him like a wolf at bay.
translation.kr: 펠리아스도 궁지에 몰린 늑대처럼 맞섰습니다.

translation.en: It was hard to tell who was stronger or fiercer.
translation.kr: 둘 중 누가 더 강하고 사나운지 우열을 가리기 힘들었습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: But after a moment Pelias spoke gently, ‘Why then so rash, my son?  You, and not I, have said what is said; why blame me for what I have not done? Had you bid me love the man of whom I spoke, and make him my son-in-law and heir, I would have obeyed you; and what if I obey you now, and send the man to win himself immortal fame?  I have not harmed you, or him. One thing at least I know, that he will go, and that gladly; for he has a hero’s heart within him, loving glory, and scorning to break the word which he has given.’

translation.en: But after a moment, Pelias spoke gently.
translation.kr: 하지만 잠시 후, 펠리아스는 부드럽게 말했습니다.

translation.en: Why so rash, my son?
translation.kr: 왜 이리 성급하게 구느냐, 아들아?

translation.en: You said the words, not I.
translation.kr: 그렇게 말한 것은 내가 아니라 너다.

translation.en: Why blame me for what I have not done?
translation.kr: 왜 내가 하지 않은 일로 나를 탓하느냐?

translation.en: Had you asked me to love that man, I would have obeyed.
translation.kr: 네가 그 사람을 아껴서 사위나 후계자로 삼으라고 했다면 난 따랐을 것이다.

translation.en: What if I obey you now and send him to win immortal fame?
translation.kr: 지금 네 말에 따라 그를 불멸의 명예를 얻을 길로 보낸다면 어떻겠느냐?

translation.en: I have harmed neither you nor him.
translation.kr: 나는 너도, 그 사람도 해치지 않았다.

translation.en: I know that he will go gladly.
translation.kr: 나는 그가 기쁜 마음으로 갈 것이란 걸 안다.

translation.en: He has a hero’s heart, loves glory, and scorns to break his word.
translation.kr: 그는 영웅의 심장을 가졌고, 영광을 사랑하며, 자신이 한 말을 어기는 것을 경멸하니까.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Jason saw that he was entrapped; but his second promise to Cheiron came into his mind, and he thought, ‘What if the Centaur were a prophet in that also, and meant that I should win the fleece!’  Then he cried aloud—

translation.en: Jason saw that he was entrapped.
translation.kr: 이아손은 자신이 덫에 걸렸음을 알았습니다.

translation.en: But his second promise to Chiron came to his mind.
translation.kr: 하지만 케이론과 한 두 번째 약속이 떠올랐습니다.

translation.en: What if the Centaur foresaw this as well?
translation.kr: 그 켄타우로스가 이 일도 내다본 것이라면? 그는 생각했습니다.

translation.en: Did he mean for me to win the fleece?
translation.kr: 내가 그 양털을 얻기를 바랐던 것일까?

translation.en: Then he cried aloud.
translation.kr: 그리고 그는 큰 소리로 외쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘You have well spoken, cunning uncle of mine!  I love glory, and I dare keep to my word.  I will go and fetch this golden fleece.  Promise me but this in return, and keep your word as I keep mine.  Treat my father lovingly while I am gone, for the sake of the all-seeing Zeus; and give me up the kingdom for my own on the day that I bring back the golden fleece.’

translation.en: You have spoken well, my cunning uncle!
translation.kr: 말씀 한 번 잘하셨습니다, 교활한 숙부님!

translation.en: I love glory, and I dare keep my word.
translation.kr: 저는 영광을 사랑하고, 제 말은 반드시 지킵니다.

translation.en: I will go and fetch this golden fleece.
translation.kr: 제가 가서 이 황금 양털을 가져오겠습니다.

translation.en: Promise me this in return, and keep your word.
translation.kr: 그 대신 숙부님도 한 가지 약속을 하고 꼭 지키십시오.

translation.en: Treat my father lovingly while I am gone.
translation.kr: 모든 것을 꿰뚫어 보시는 제우스를 걸고, 제가 없는 동안 아버지를 잘 보살펴 주십시오.

translation.en: And give the kingdom to me on the day I bring the fleece.
translation.kr: 그리고 제가 황금 양털을 가져오는 날, 이 왕국을 제게 넘겨주십시오.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: Then Pelias looked at him and almost loved him, in the midst of all his hate; and said, ‘I promise, and I will perform.  It will be no shame to give up my kingdom to the man who wins that fleece.’  Then they swore a great oath between them; and afterwards both went in, and lay down to sleep.

translation.en: Pelias looked at him and almost loved him, despite his hate.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 그를 쳐다보며, 자신의 증오 속에서도 그를 향한 애정을 느낄 뻔했습니다.

translation.en: I promise, and I will perform, he said.
translation.kr: 약속하마, 그리고 반드시 지킬 것이다, 라고 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: It is no shame to yield to the man who wins that fleece.
translation.kr: 그 양털을 얻어 온 사내에게 왕국을 물려주는 것은 전혀 부끄러운 일이 아니니까.

translation.en: Then they swore a great oath between them.
translation.kr: 그리고 그들은 굳게 맹세했습니다.

translation.en: Afterward, both went in and lay down to sleep.
translation.kr: 그 후 두 사람은 안으로 들어가 잠자리에 들었습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: But Jason could not sleep for thinking of his mighty oath, and how he was to fulfil it, all alone, and without wealth or friends.  So he tossed a long time upon his bed, and thought of this plan and of that; and sometimes Phrixus seemed to call him, in a thin voice, faint and low, as if it came from far across the sea, ‘Let me come home to my fathers and have rest.’  And sometimes he seemed to see the eyes of Hera, and to hear her words again—‘Call on me in the hour of need, and see if the Immortals can forget.’

translation.en: But Jason could not sleep for thinking of his mighty oath.
translation.kr: 하지만 이아손은 자신의 엄청난 맹세에 대해 생각하느라 잠을 이룰 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: He wondered how to fulfill it without wealth or friends.
translation.kr: 돈도 친구도 없이 홀로 어떻게 그 맹세를 지킬지 고민했습니다.

translation.en: He tossed for a long time on his bed, thinking of many plans.
translation.kr: 그는 침대에서 오랫동안 뒤척이며 이런저런 계획을 떠올렸습니다.

translation.en: Sometimes Phrixus seemed to call him in a faint voice.
translation.kr: 가끔은 프릭소스가 희미하고 낮은 목소리로 그를 부르는 것 같았습니다.

translation.en: It sounded as if it came from far across the sea.
translation.kr: 마치 바다 건너 멀리서 들려오는 소리 같았습니다.

translation.en: Let me come home to my fathers and have rest.
translation.kr: 나를 조상들의 고향으로 데려가 편히 쉬게 해다오.

translation.en: Sometimes he seemed to see the eyes of Hera.
translation.kr: 때로는 헤라 여신의 눈이 보이는 듯했습니다.

translation.en: He heard her words again.
translation.kr: 그녀의 목소리가 다시 들렸습니다.

translation.en: Call on me in the hour of need.
translation.kr: 어려운 일이 생기면 나를 부르거라.

translation.en: See if the immortals can forget.
translation.kr: 신들이 은혜를 잊는지 아닌지 알게 될 것이다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: And on the morrow he went to Pelias, and said, ‘Give me a victim, that I may sacrifice to Hera.’  So he went up, and offered his sacrifice; and as he stood by the altar Hera sent a thought into his mind; and he went back to Pelias, and said—

translation.en: On the next day, he went to Pelias.
translation.kr: 다음 날, 그는 펠리아스에게 갔습니다.

translation.en: Give me a victim to sacrifice to Hera, he said.
translation.kr: 헤라 여신께 제물로 바칠 짐승을 주십시오, 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: So he went up and offered his sacrifice.
translation.kr: 그는 위로 올라가 제물을 바쳤습니다.

translation.en: As he stood by the altar, Hera sent a thought into his mind.
translation.kr: 그가 제단 옆에 서 있을 때, 헤라 여신이 그의 마음속에 한 가지 생각을 불어넣었습니다.

translation.en: He went back to Pelias and spoke.
translation.kr: 그는 다시 펠리아스에게 돌아가 말했습니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: ‘If you are indeed in earnest, give me two heralds, that they may go round to all the princes of the Minuai, who were pupils of the Centaur with me, that we may fit out a ship together, and take what shall befall.’

translation.en: If you are truly in earnest, give me two heralds.
translation.kr: 숙부님이 정말 진심이시라면 제게 두 명의 전령을 주십시오.

translation.en: They can go to all the princes of the Minyans.
translation.kr: 전령들이 저와 함께 케이론의 제자였던 미니아이족의 모든 왕자들에게 가게 해주십시오.

translation.en: We will fit out a ship together and face whatever comes.
translation.kr: 우리가 함께 배를 준비하여 어떤 운명이든 맞설 수 있도록 말입니다.

part: Part II: How Jason Lost His Sandal in Anauros
raw: At that Pelias praised his wisdom, and hastened to send the heralds out; for he said in his heart, ‘Let all the princes go with him, and, like him, never return; for so I shall be lord of all the Minuai, and the greatest king in Hellas.’

translation.en: Pelias praised his wisdom and hurried to send the heralds.
translation.kr: 펠리아스는 그의 지혜를 칭찬하며 서둘러 전령들을 보냈습니다.

translation.en: For he said in his heart.
translation.kr: 그는 속으로 이렇게 생각했기 때문입니다.

translation.en: Let all the princes go with him and never return.
translation.kr: 모든 왕자들이 그와 함께 떠나 영영 돌아오지 않기를.

translation.en: Then I will be lord of all the Minyans.
translation.kr: 그러면 내가 모든 미니아이족의 주인이 될 것이다.

translation.en: I will be the greatest king in Hellas.
translation.kr: 그리고 헬라스에서 가장 위대한 왕이 될 것이다.
